messages.content:
You are an experienced teacher of introductory C programming. A student wrote the function below for a task. Decide which single label best describes the student's code. Labels:
M01: Loop runs one step too many or too few. The student believes: i<=n (from 0) runs n times; whether the bound is the last value included or excluded is mixed up
M02: Loop variable never moves toward the exit. The student believes: The loop variable advances by itself and the loop ends by itself
M03: Running total is reset inside the loop. The student believes: The total keeps its value across passes even if it is set again inside the loop
M04: int ÷ int drops the decimals. The student believes: int / int gives the exact decimal
M05: Variable used before it was given a value. The student believes: Local variables start at 0
M06: `=` stores a value; `==` compares. The student believes: = compares
M07: A stray `;` gives the if/loop an empty body. The student believes: A ; after the header is harmless
M08: Arrays start at 0; last cell is n−1. The student believes: Arrays are indexed 1..n
M10: `printf` shows a value; `return` hands it back. The student believes: Printing the value hands it back to the caller
D01: The search gives up after the first miss. The student believes: The else branch means 'not this one, keep looking'; it doesn't end or overwrite anything
D02: Binary search window never shrinks (`low = mid`). The student believes: mid is excluded from the window automatically
D03: Swapping without a temp loses a value. The student believes: Two assignments happen at the same time
D04: One pass doesn't sort the whole array. The student believes: One pass over the array sorts it
D05: Recursion has no reachable base case. The student believes: Recursion stops by itself when the work is done
D06: The recursive call doesn't move toward the base case. The student believes: The recursive call moves toward the base case on its own
D07: The recursive call's result is thrown away. The student believes: The recursive call's result is combined automatically
D08: `==` doesn't compare text in C. The student believes: == compares text
CORRECT: the program solves the task correctly (even if the style is unusual).
OTHER: the program is wrong or odd, but none of the 17 beliefs above explains it.
Answer with a JSON object {"label": "<one label id>", "reason": "<one short sentence>"} and nothing else.

content: {"label": "M01", "reason": "The loop condition position <= n runs one step too many, accessing cells[n] out of bounds; it should be position < n."}

parsed.label: M01
parsed.reason: The loop condition position <= n runs one step too many, accessing cells[n] out of bounds; it should be position < n.
